title: Haiku Explained
description:
Haiku is not a cheaper model. It is a model built for steps where the answer is already obvious before the reasoning starts.

Sorting an inbound message into a category requires reading and pattern matching. Routing that message to the right team requires applying a rule. Pulling structured data from a form requires extraction. None of these tasks involve uncertainty. The correct output is deterministic given the input, which means spending reasoning capacity on them is waste, not thoroughness.

The automation in this example makes the decision visible. An inbound message comes in, Haiku reads it, identifies whether it belongs to sales, support, spam, or a fallback category, and routes it accordingly. No response gets written. No judgment call gets made. The step runs, the output is a category label, and the next step in the workflow picks up from there.

Haiku handles the obvious steps so Sonnet and Opus can be reserved for the ones that actually require reasoning.
